quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light warns you that a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and make your turn there.
Safely change lanes then put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and make your turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. Drive to the next intersection and make your turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Get out of the car and go for help.
Lay down in your car and go to sleep.
Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.
Stay in your car. You are most likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are most likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car and wait for help. Rescuers will find you more easily if you stay with your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is unsafe.

questions.question: It is dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely because:

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely is dangerous because you need time and space to avoid a crash if the motorcyclist stops suddenly.

questions.question: A stop sign is shaped like a(n):
questions.explanation: Stop signs are eight-sided. Only stop signs have this octagonal shape. All eight-sided signs tell drivers to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Use tires with proper air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your car slides on a layer of water between the tires and road. Low air pressure, bad tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean:

options.text: Passing is not permitted from either direction.
Passing is permitted from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not permitted from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction. You may only cross them to turn left or pass pedestrians, bicyclists, and scooter riders when it is safe.

questions.question: A good rule to remember for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Try to get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases collision risk. Drive with traffic flow within the speed limit and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Pavement is especially slippery right after rain starts.
Give yourself extra space when stopping.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery, especially right after rain begins. Slow down in heavy rain or when water is on the road to prevent your wheels from losing grip.

questions.question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to speed up than smaller vehicles. They lose speed going uphill. Give trucks extra space, especially on inclines.

questions.question: If you are under 18, what must you do to get a probationary license?

options.text: Have an instruction permit for at least six months.
Have no moving traffic violations in the past six months.
Complete an approved driver education course.

questions.explanation: To get a probationary license if you are under 18, you must: complete an approved driver education course, have an instruction permit for at least six months, get 30 hours of supervised driving (including 10 hours at night), have no moving traffic violations in the past six months, pass a driving skills test, and pay required fees.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They are not affected by speed.

questions.explanation: Stopping distances are longer and crashes are more severe when you drive faster.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Keep the wheels off the pavement and reduce your speed by gently applying the brakes. When you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not sharply turn the wheel to force your vehicle back onto the road.

questions.question: How should you warn other drivers when you need to stop or slow down unexpectedly?

options.text: Wave your left arm out the window.
Quickly tap the brake pedal several times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Quickly tap the brake pedal several times.
questions.explanation: Quickly tap your brake pedal three or four times. Your brake lights will tell other drivers you are slowing down.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Drive faster to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If you cannot see ahead, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: How can you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down. If possible, change lanes to stay away from the stopped emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If possible, change lanes to stay away from the stopped emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside help vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. If you cannot change lanes safely or there is only one lane, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means the action is prohibited. U-turns are not permitted where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What headlights should you use in fog, rain, or snow?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect back in bad weather and create glare that makes it hard to see.

questions.question: What should you do when it starts to rain while driving?

options.text: Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Drive close behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: When heavy rain reduces visibility, slow down. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If the rain is too heavy to see clearly, pull off the road and stop until it clears.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield to you.
You must yield to the pedestrian.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must always yield the right-of-way to them.

questions.question: What must you do at a green arrow?

options.text: Yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. But first, you must yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection. Then turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: When driving at night, what should you do?

options.text: Stay farther behind the car ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see. Increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react. Use your headlights properly. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights as the glare can blind you.

questions.question: An oncoming car has its high beams on and is blinding you. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have much bigger blind spots than regular cars.
You can see all blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have much bigger blind spots than regular cars.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots, even with mirrors. Mirrors cannot show everything. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than most passenger cars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you that you cannot drive in that direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: What do downward-pointing triangle signs mean?
questions.explanation: Downward-pointing triangle signs tell drivers to yield. Wait until the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians, then you can proceed.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and drive with caution.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Drive closer to the car ahead of you.
Drive carefully and do not slow down to look at things.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully and do not slow down to look at things.
questions.explanation: Do not "rubberneck" or slow down to look at unusual things in construction zones. This causes traffic to back up. Just drive through the zone carefully.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are breaking the law.
Only give pedestrians the right-of-way when they have the legal right to it.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are breaking the law.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. It is your responsibility to watch for pedestrians and let them cross, even if they are jaywalking.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At the same speed as freeway traffic or close to it.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the same speed as freeway traffic or close to it.
questions.explanation: Match the speed of freeway traffic when you merge, unless the traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: On a hill or in a curve because few cars are coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If you are next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane ahead is clear.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming cars. Never drive on the shoulder to pass. You cannot cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean that passing is:
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross the center to pass, no matter which direction they are going.

questions.question: You may cross double solid yellow lines:
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into a driveway, enter or exit a highway, or make a U-turn where it is legal.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow down to the freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see what is ahead, and braking inside a curve can cause your car to skid.

questions.question: If you drive much slower than other traffic, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and get a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slower when there is heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive too slowly and block traffic, you can get a ticket. Match the speed of traffic unless traffic exceeds the speed limit.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign says you cannot turn right.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and drive carefully at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be careful, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If a bus is signaling to return to the main road after stopping, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.explanation: When a bus signals to return to the road after picking up or dropping off passengers, you must yield. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beam headlights on. This helps other drivers see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: You can pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street only if:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.

questions.explanation: You can pass safely only if you can see the road clearly, return to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what lights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction will become one lane.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your lane only when you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough safe space in front of the other vehicle.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Do not worry because all vehicles work the same way.
Do not tell your friend that you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Spend a few minutes learning where the controls are and how they work before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes learning where the controls are and how they work before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, take a few minutes to learn where the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn are located and how they work. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: If you see an "Exit only" sign above your lane, what must you do?

options.text: You can either continue through the interchange or exit from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue through the interchange.
You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means that lane will not continue through the interchange. You must either change lanes or exit the freeway.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Letting their cars run in the driveway.

questions.explanation: Every quick stop uses fuel to accelerate again. By looking ahead and slowing down gradually or changing lanes, you can avoid unnecessary braking and save gas.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your vision, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.
